Abel.d: Abel, the second son of Adam

Cain.d: Cain, the first son of Adam

Euphrates.d: the Euphrates, a river of Eden

Henoch.d: Henoch, a son of Cain; also a son of Jared

Hevilath.d: Hevilath, a land the Phison encircles

Lamech.d: Lamech, a descendant of Cain; also the father of Noë

Noë.d: Noë, the builder of the ark

Seth.d: Seth, the third son of Adam

Tigris.d: the Tigris, a river of Eden

adsum, adesse, adfui.d: to be present, to be at hand

benedico, benedicere, benedixi, benedict.d: to bless, to speak well of

consurgo, consurgere, consurrexi, consur.d: to rise up, to stand up

deambulo, deambulare, deambulavi, deambu.d: to walk about, to take a walk

egredior, egredi, egressus sum.d: to go out, to go forth

emitto, emittere, emisi, emissus.d: to send out, to send away

immitto, immittere, immisi, immissus.d: to send in, to let in

indico, indicare, indicavi, indicatus.d: to point out, to make known

induco, inducere, induxi, inductus.d: to lead in, to bring in

insidior, insidiari, insidiatus sum.d: to lie in wait, to plot against

ipse, ipsa, ipsum.d: himself, herself, itself; the very one

irascor, irasci, iratus sum.d: to be angry, to grow angry

maledico, maledicere, maledixi, maledict.d: to curse, to speak ill of

nequaquam.d: by no means, not at all

nescio, nescire, nescivi, nescitus.d: not to know, to be ignorant of

pario, parere, peperi, partus.d: to bring forth, to give birth to

præsum, præesse, præfui.d: to be over, to preside over

respicio, respicere, respexi, respectus.d: to look back at, to regard
